items.originalTitle: Jim Cramer Says Goldman's SpaceX Price Target Hike Proves It Wasn't Guesswork
items.originalSummary: Jim Cramer says Goldman Sachs' $10 SpaceX price target hike to $230 shows its earlier $220 was not guesswork. The CNBC Mad Money host sees analysts moving ahead of the stock instead of chasing it. Goldman, a lead underwriter on SpaceX's June initial public offering (IPO), opened coverage at $205 in July under analyst Eric Sheridan. The $230 target is its second raise since. Cramer said the $220 target looked hard to defend when SpaceX shares sat near $120. Since then, SpaceX has climbed, closing at $171.92 on October 6, according to Google Finance. "Maybe there really is some rigor to the analysis." He says analysts covering speculative stocks rarely lift targets until buyers have already pushed shares past the old one. Goldman's note cites higher expected AI capacity, revenue and margins. Cramer links that to demand for SpaceX's rented AI computing, which he says explains its $40 billion chip plan.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 Closes Dragon Hatch, Preps for Departure
historyItems.originalSummary: NASA's SpaceX Crew-12 members gather for a portrait in the pressure suits they will wear when they depart the International Space Station inside the SpaceX Dragon spacecraft. From left, Roscosmos cosmonaut and mission specialist Andrey Fedyaev, NASA astronauts Jack Hathaway and Jessica Meir, Crew-12 pilot and commander respectively, and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut and mission specialist Sophie Adenot.NASA and SpaceX are targeting no earlier than 8:05 a.m. EDT, Wednesday, Oct. 7, for the undocking of the agency's SpaceX Crew-12 mission from the International Space Station, pending weather conditions.An Oct. 7 undock puts NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev on schedule to splash down off the coast of California at approximately 11:34 a.m. on Thursday, Oct. 8.NASA's live Crew-12 return coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:https://www.nasa.gov/liveMission managers continue monitoring conditions in the recovery area, as undocking of the SpaceX Dragon depends on spacecraft readiness, recovery team readiness, weather conditions in the Pacific off the coast of California, and other factors.NASA's coverage is as follows (all times Eastern and subject to change based on real-time operations):Wednesday, Oct. 76 a.m.: Hatch closure coverage begins6:20 a.m.: Hatch closing7:45 a.m.: Undocking coverage begins8:05 a.m.: UndockingFollowing the conclusion of undocking coverage, NASA will provide audio-only communications between Crew-12, the space station, and flight controllers during Dragon's transit away from the orbital complex.Thursday, Oct. 810:20 a.m.: Return coverage begins10:46 a.m.: Deorbit burn11:34 a.m.: Splashdown1:15 p.m.: International Space Station briefing for Crew-12 return and SpaceX Commercial Resupply Services-35 launch with the following participants:Bill Spetch, deputy manager of Commercial, NASA's Low Earth Orbit ProgramDr. Liz Warren, deputy chief scientist, NASA's Low Earth Orbit ProgramLee Echerd, senior mission manager, Customer Operations and Integration, SpaceXAndreas Mogensen, leader, Human Exploration Group, ESATo participate virtually in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson newsroom for call details by 12 p.m., Oct. 8, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. The agency's media credentialing policy is available online.For more information about the Crew-12 mission, visit:https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-12end-Joshua Finch / Jimi RussellHeadquarters, Washington202-358-1100joshua.a.finch@nasa.gov / james.j.russell@nasa.govSandra Jones / Joseph ZakrzewskiJohnson Space Center, Houston281-483-5111sandra.p.jones@nasa.gov / joseph.a.zakrzewski@nasa.govSteve SiceloffKennedy Space Center, Fla.321-867-2468steven.p.siceloff@nasa.gov(C) 2026 Electronic News Publishing, source ENP Newswire

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne enhances Titan HP for AI chip reliability tests
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne, Inc. announced a production-ready system that delivers enhanced burn-in capabilities on its Titan? HP platform. Traditional burn-in holds devices in banks of dedicated ovens at a controlled air temperature for hours before they move on to functional test.Teradyne Titan HP instead holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, so reliability stress functions are optimized and thermal controls are enabled at the per-device level. Titan HP can be used for system level test or reliability testing, optimizing capital cost investments. For reliability testing, every device carries its full stress-and-test history on a single record.Per-site thermal control, tuned to each device's thermal and force zones, and paired with high per-device kilowatt power delivery, lets Titan HP sustain reliability-stress conditions on parts whose power draw and heat dissipation strain a conventional oven flow. The platform's asynchronous slot architecture loads and tests each slot independently, so a long stress run on one device does not idle the rest of the system, and individual sites can be serviced while the system continues to operate. Test programs run on the Teradyne Atlas software platform, which lets engineers import existing programs or build new ones and port them to other Teradyne system level test systems. Burn-in has long been standard for automotive and other high-reliability silicon.AI accelerators and cloud infrastructure devices are now entering the same category, driven by the high cost of a single failed accelerator in a deployed rack. Enhanced burn-in extends Teradyne?s test portfolio, which spans the AI device supply chain from wafer to data center.

historyItems.originalTitle: Marvell raises 2028 revenue forecast on strong AI data center demand
historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell raised its 2028 revenue forecast to about $20 billion on Tuesday, citing strong demand for its chips used in data centers.Shares of the company rose nearly 9% in early trading. The stock has more than tripled in value so far this year.Marvell had forecast $18 billion in revenue in August. Analysts were expecting revenue of $18.2 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.

historyItems.originalTitle: Marvell stock surges after company raises 2028 revenue outlook to $20 billion
historyItems.originalSummary: Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a data-center connectivity and custom AI chipmaker, closed at $287.01, up 5.81%. Investors were reacting to Investor Day guidance that lifted near- and long-term revenue targets, and they are watching custom AI growth next. Trading volume reached 50.1 million shares, coming in about 122% above its three-month average of 22.6 million shares. Marvell Technology IPO'd in 2000 and has grown 1,927% since going public.

historyItems.originalTitle: AMD plans to substantially increase supply in 2027, CEO says
historyItems.originalSummary: AMD plans to increase its chip supply in 2027 as the company works to keep pace with demand for artificial intelligence hardware, chair and CEO Lisa Su said Tuesday, according to Reuters . "We've been able to increase our supply as we've gone through 2026, and we're going to substantially increase our supply in 2027, but we can definitely use more," Su told reporters in Taipei.

historyItems.summary: 在 6 月中旬 IPO 後的最初幾天達到高點後，SpaceX SPCX 股價大幅下跌，截至 7 月底下跌了約 48%。然而，自8月初以來，這家航空航太公司的股價卻出現逆轉，反彈約58%。摩根士丹利週日對 MS 的看漲呼籲增強了 SPCX 的勢頭，週一股價上漲約 7.7%，達到 6 月中旬以來的最高水平。 SPCX 週二盤前上漲約 0.40%。
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX jumps to highest close since June on bullish Morgan Stanley call
historyItems.originalSummary: After reaching highs in the initial days following its mid-June IPO, SpaceX SPCX shares fell sharply, declining about 48% through late July. However, since the start of August, the aerospace company's stock has turned the tables, rebounding about 58%. Morgan Stanley's MS bullish call on Sunday added to SPCX's momentum, with shares rising about 7.7% on Monday to their highest level since mid-June. SPCX rose about 0.40% during pre-market hours on Tuesday.

historyItems.originalTitle: KLA (KLAC) Stock Looks Rich As Revenue Guidance Rises
historyItems.originalSummary: In recent days, KLA Corporation has attracted renewed attention as analysts highlighted its essential process-control role in easing the chip shortage and supporting AI-focused semiconductor manufacturing, while also pointing to ongoing risks from U.S. export restrictions and cyclical wafer equipment spending. At the same time, upward revisions to earnings estimates and commentary about KLA's differentiated tools for advanced packaging and complex chip designs have reinforced the company's importance to AI infrastructure build-outs, even as investors weigh exposure to tariffs, component costs, and concentrated customer demand. We'll now examine how this stronger analyst sentiment around KLA's critical AI-related process-control demand reshapes and reinforces its existing investment narrative.

historyItems.summary: 伯明罕市長蘭德爾·伍德芬(Randall Woodfin)在他的妻子和她的房地產公司因與擬議的伯明罕資料中心訴訟有關的發現糾紛中被點名後進行了反擊。伍德芬週三在 Facebook 上發布的聲明中表示，他的妻子肯德拉·伍德芬 (Kendra Woodfin) 和她的公司 Iron City Premier Realty 沒有參與計劃建設 Nebius 數據中心的房產的購買或出售。 「我們又來了，」伍德芬說。 “這是一個赤裸裸的謊言。
historyItems.originalTitle: Homeowners seek subpoena for mayor’s wife’s realty company in Nebius data center suit
historyItems.originalSummary: Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin is pushing back after his wife and her real-estate company were named in a discovery dispute tied to a lawsuit over a proposed Birmingham data center. In a statement posted to Facebook Wednesday, Woodfin said his wife, Kendra Woodfin, and her company, Iron City Premier Realty, had no involvement in the purchase or sale of the property where the Nebius data center is planned. “Here we go again,” Woodfin said. “This is a bald-faced lie. “My wife and her business had nothing to do with this property. She had no part in the purchase. No part in the sale. No connection to this litigation. There isn't a shred of evidence that says otherwise, because there's nothing to find. She wasn't involved. Period.” The comments follow an Oct. 6 filing in Jefferson County Circuit Court in which Iron City objected to a proposed subpoena from homeowners challenging the data-center project. Iron City said it “had no involvement” in the acquisition, purchase, sale, conveyance, financing, brokerage, development, zoning, permitting or closing of the property identified in the subpoena. The company also argued the subpoena is overly broad and that the plaintiffs have not established a factual basis connecting Iron City to the transaction. The court has not ruled on the objections. Woodfin also emphasized that his wife is a private citizen and has no role in Birmingham's zoning or permitting decisions. “She is a business owner. She is the mother of our children. She is a private citizen. She has never held office in this city. She doesn't vote on zoning. She doesn't sign permits. She doesn't sit on the Zoning Board of Adjustment or the City Council,” he said. Woodfin accused the attorneys behind the filing of intentionally putting his wife's business name into the case because of her relationship to him. “They wanted a headline,” he said. “Everybody knows how politically charged and unpopular data centers are. That's the play. You put a name in a court filing. Reporters read court filings. The story writes itself: ‘Mayor's wife named in data center lawsuit.’” Woodfin said he plans to pursue legal options to protect his wife's reputation. “We are going to be as aggressive as possible, exploring every legal recourse available to protect my wife's good name and the professional reputation of her business. This won't be the last you hear about it.” The mayor said he is accustomed to criticism but does not want his wife drawn into political disputes. “Come at me all day. I've been taking hits for nine years, and I'll take plenty more. That's the job I signed up for. My wife didn't. And I won't let her become collateral damage in a political hit designed to get at me.” The underlying lawsuit was filed by homeowners Robert B. Sansome and Gail Sansome against Hoar Construction LLC, Lakeshore Data Center LLC, Nebius Inc. and the City of Birmingham. The case remains in discovery, with a non-jury trial scheduled for March 8, 2027. A judge is scheduled to hear arguments Wednesday on objections involving subpoenas. The latest filings do not establish that Kendra Woodfin or Iron City Premier Realty participated in the property transactions at issue.

historyItems.originalTitle: Kratos Reports More Than $100M in Contracts for Space Intelligence Data
historyItems.originalSummary: SAN DIEGO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced multiple contract awards totaling over $100 million to develop prototype mission applications and cyber capabilities providing space intelligence data in support of joint operations across the space and cyberspace domains. Work under the contracts will provide warfighters with capabilities to collect and process complex radio frequency (RF) signals, develop intelligence on the operational environment and support the joint targeting cycle – the process used to identify, prioritize and target assets. The prototype systems will support electronic warfare and offensive cyber operations, including capabilities for access and battle damage assessment. The work leverages the KnownSpace ® Network, Kratos’ global RF collection infrastructure consisting of more than 190 strategically placed sensors around the world, along with RF data and capabilities provided by KnownSpace Recon+™, Kratos’ field-portable space domain awareness (SDA) terminals. In addition, the contracts will leverage Kratos’ software products, analytics and expertise in RF, signal processing, cybersecurity and software development, establishing a proven technology base that can be adapted and integrated to meet emerging space and cyber mission requirements. “Kratos brings decades of space experience together with proven commercial technology and agile engineering to solve some of today’s most complex mission challenges,” said Greg Caicedo, Senior Vice President at Kratos . “Our systems, software and hardware support missions across SDA, command & control, satellite operations and cybersecurity. By building on proven technology and rapidly adapting it to emerging mission needs, we can deliver new capabilities faster and keep pace as the space environment changes.” The Kratos KnownSpace family of SDA products and services which support these awards provide deep insights for global, sovereign, and tactical operations. Built on more than 30 years of satellite monitoring and RF expertise, the KnownSpace family combines global RF sensing, software, managed operations and deployable systems to detect, characterize and understand satellite and terrestrial activity. Solutions include enterprise software applications, portable form factors that can be deployed anywhere and persistent global RF signal monitoring and geolocation through its KnownSpace Network of over 20 locations and 190 sensors worldwide—the largest commercially owned, commercially operated (COCO) RF sensor network.

historyItems.summary: 馬薩諸塞州北雷丁和舊金山，2026 年 10 月 5 日（環球通訊社）——自動化測試設備和先進機器人系統的領先供應商 Teradyne, Inc.（納斯達克股票代碼：TER）和將人工智能和數據中心基礎設施生產推向邊緣的下一代製造商 Bright Machines, Inc. 今天宣布泰瑞達對 Bright Machines 進行戰略投資。
historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Partners with Bright Machines to Put Robots, Test Tech in AI Infrastructure Microfactories
historyItems.originalSummary: NORTH READING, Mass. and SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER), a leading provider of automated test equipment and advanced robotics systems, and Bright Machines, Inc., a next-generation manufacturer bringing AI and data center infrastructure production to the edge, today announced a strategic investment by Teradyne in Bright Machines. The investment accompanies a strategic collaboration focused on integrating Teradyne robotics and test technologies with Bright Machines’ software-defined manufacturing platform and advancing AI infrastructure manufacturing. AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest electronics manufacturing buildouts in recent history. As hyperscalers, AI laboratories, silicon providers, and OEMs invest in next-generation compute, manufacturing has become a determinant of deployment speed, quality, and economic value, and manufacturers place a premium on lines that can be reconfigured in software as product designs refresh. Teradyne works with manufacturers across that ecosystem, including EMS and ODM providers, OEMs, and hyperscalers, supplying the robotics and test technologies that make high-mix, high-value electronics production possible. Bright Machines brings a unique software-defined manufacturing platform spanning design, robotics, automation, inspection, material movement, production intelligence, and operations, with a history of more than 130 microfactory deployments across 10+ countries and, today, active AI infrastructure production in the United States. "Physical AI is changing what is possible on the factory floor, and Teradyne and Bright Machines are partnering to accelerate this evolution," said Shantnu Sharma, chief development officer, Teradyne. "The combination of Bright Machines depth in software-defined manufacturing, and Teradyne’s decades of experience in robotics and test gives companies building AI infrastructure a faster path from design into production, with data behind every unit they build."

historyItems.originalTitle: Should You Buy AST SpaceMobile Stock While It's Trading Below $60?
historyItems.originalSummary: In the past few days, law firms Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP and Rosen Law Firm announced securities class action lawsuits against AST SpaceMobile, alleging misleading statements about its capital resources, competitive position and user adoption between March 4, 2025 and July 15, 2026. The cases focus on whether AST SpaceMobile misrepresented its balance of cash, debt and share issuance while scaling its satellite network, raising fresh questions about how robust its funding model really was during this critical buildout phase. We will now examine how these securities fraud allegations around capital requirements and user adoption may reshape AST SpaceMobile's earlier investment narrative.

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Makes Strategic Investment in Bright Machines to Advance AI Infrastructure Manufacturing
historyItems.originalSummary: NORTH READING, Mass. and SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER), a leading provider of automated test equipment and advanced robotics systems, and Bright Machines, Inc., a next-generation manufacturer bringing AI and data center infrastructure production to the edge, today announced a strategic investment by Teradyne in Bright Machines. The investment accompanies a strategic collaboration focused on integrating Teradyne robotics and test technologies with Bright Machines’ software-defined manufacturing platform and advancing AI infrastructure manufacturing. AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest electronics manufacturing buildouts in recent history. As hyperscalers, AI laboratories, silicon providers, and OEMs invest in next-generation compute, manufacturing has become a determinant of deployment speed, quality, and economic value, and manufacturers place a premium on lines that can be reconfigured in software as product designs refresh. Teradyne works with manufacturers across that ecosystem, including EMS and ODM providers, OEMs, and hyperscalers, supplying the robotics and test technologies that make high-mix, high-value electronics production possible. Bright Machines brings a unique software-defined manufacturing platform spanning design, robotics, automation, inspection, material movement, production intelligence, and operations, with a history of more than 130 microfactory deployments across 10+ countries and, today, active AI infrastructure production in the United States. "Physical AI is changing what is possible on the factory floor, and Teradyne and Bright Machines are partnering to accelerate this evolution," said Shantnu Sharma, chief development officer, Teradyne. "The combination of Bright Machines depth in software-defined manufacturing, and Teradyne’s decades of experience in robotics and test gives companies building AI infrastructure a faster path from design into production, with data behind every unit they build."

The company’s substrate wafers are used when a typical silicon substrate wafer cannot meet the performance requirements of a semiconductor or optoelectronic device. End markets include AI/data center connectivity, 5G infrastructure, passive optical networks, LED lighting, lasers, sensors, power amplifiers for wireless devices and satellite solar cells. AXT’s worldwide headquarters are in Fremont, California where the company maintains sales, administration and customer service functions. AXT has its Asia headquarters in Beijing, China and manufacturing facilities in three separate locations in China. In addition, as part of its supply chain strategy, the company has partial ownership in over ten companies in China producing raw materials for its manufacturing process. historyItems.summary: Vistra (VST) 在向聯邦能源監管委員會提交的一份新文件中對 PJM 的臨時資源充足服務提案提出質疑，認為該框架具有歧視性、存在法律缺陷，並可能擾亂 PJM 地區未來的投資信號。瑞致達對 PJM 的抵制之際，該股的交易價格為 144.89 美元，1 天股價回報率為 3.48%，7 天股價回報率為 4.98%。年初至今的股價回報率下降了12.31%，1年股東總回報率下降了27.28%，而3年股東總回報率約為起點的4.7倍。這表明，隨著投資者權衡新的監管風險與既定的價值創造歷史，近幾個月來強勁的長期勢頭已經冷卻。
historyItems.originalTitle: Vistra (VST) Could Be 52% Undervalued As $4 Billion DOE Loan Backs Nuclear Upgrades
historyItems.originalSummary: Vistra (VST) has challenged PJM's Interim Resource Adequacy Service proposal in a fresh filing with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, arguing the framework is discriminatory, legally flawed, and could disrupt future investment signals in the PJM region. Vistra's pushback at PJM comes as the stock trades at US$144.89, with a 1-day share price return of 3.48% and a 7-day share price return of 4.98%. The year-to-date share price return is down 12.31% and the 1-year total shareholder return is down 27.28%, while the 3-year total shareholder return is roughly 4.7x the starting point. This points to strong longer term momentum that has cooled in recent months as investors weigh fresh regulatory risk against an established history of value creation.

historyItems.originalTitle: Latest Injury Update on Texans WR Tank Dell Isn't Too Promising
historyItems.originalSummary: The wait for Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell continues. KPRC 2’s Aaron Wilson noted that it is currently “not the plan” to have Dell back following Week 4 against the Dallas Cowboys, the earliest he can return. Moreover, Wilson said Dell will not return “unless he can run at speed they want him to run at.” None of that is new from Wilson or the Texans. However, the insider did provide a rather dour outlook for Dell. “It is a serious injury, and he is not there yet, and they also don’t have a home for him at this point with the other receivers they have up. They’ve given us no timeline,” Wilson said during a live stream on October 2. “I’ve checked on this. It’s not imminent. I can tell you that. If it happens–if it happens–it’s later in the season.” Dell has not played since Week 16 of the 2024 season. https://twitter.com/Clay_HTXSports/status/2106128199990280418 He was a top target for Texans quarterback and draft classmate C.J. Stroud. However, the Texans have since added Kayshon Boutte (who replaces injured 2025 second-round pick Jayden Higgins in the lineup) and Jaylin Noel since Dell last played. They still have Nico Collins at the top of the pecking order. Bigger-bodied targets Xavier Hutchinson and Jared Wayne have also earned more opportunities in Dell’s absence. That is not to say any of them would play ahead of a fully healthy Dell. Part of his return process, though, will certainly include rebuilding the on-field chemistry and timing with Stroud and the offense. That is in addition to proving that he is still a superior option to some of his teammates in the passing game. Dell is also in the final year of his rookie contract. That only adds to the uncertainty around his future with the Texans. The former Houston Cougars star was supposed to play in the preseason, per DeMeco Ryans. “We’ve taken our time to kind of ramp them up slowly. So, our first week he was just on the side still, working, just some individual stuff with his position coach at the practice. And now, this past week, he got into routes on air. He got into group install. And yesterday, for the first time, he was able to get in the team drills,” Ryans said on SiriusXM NFL Radio in August. “We’ll keep giving him a little bit more every day. Planning for him to, hopefully, get out there preseason–in one of these preseason games coming up–and then be ready to go for the season.” https://twitter.com/JacobBarzilla/status/2078958050828755097 At the time, Ryans noted how proud he was of Dell’s comeback journey. For the situation to go from that sort of optimism to the more dour tones it has taken on now is disappointing. It is even more so given the kind of boost a healthy Dell could provide the 0-3 Texans. Instead, they will continue to bide their time without him. Meanwhile, he must continue working to prove he can be the same player he was for the Texans before his latest devastating injury two years ago.

historyItems.originalTitle: Is Sovereign AI Partnership Altering The Investment Case For Cisco (CSCO)?
historyItems.originalSummary: In late September 2026, Bell Canada and Cisco announced a memorandum of understanding to build a sovereign AI infrastructure platform in Canada, combining Bell's domestic data centres and networks with Cisco's AI, security, observability, and Sovereign Critical Infrastructure technologies for customers with strict data residency and control needs. historyItems.originalTitle: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. (AAOI) latest stock news and headlines
historyItems.originalSummary: Applied Optoelectronics, Inc. introduced new AI-driven capabilities within the platform that enable operators to turn visibility into immediate action. QuantumLink Central's AI doesn't stop at finding network issues. It acts on them.When it detects a performance problem, it recommends and applies adjustments that keep the rest of the network stable until a permanent fix is made. Operators stay in control and approve each change before it is applied. QuantumLink Central uses AI to detect impairments and pinpoint where they are coming from, remotely and automatically.This cuts troubleshooting time and truck rolls. QuantumLink Central gives operators a clear, real-time view of the health of their whole network. AI-driven health insights help teams quickly see where attention is needed most.They can then prioritize their work and move from reactive troubleshooting to proactive network management. QuantumLink Central uses AI to spot developing issues before they affect subscribers. It forecasts potential faults and tells operators how confident it is in each forecast and how much lead time they have.Maintenance can then be planned, instead of carried out as an emergency. Front and center is a first-of-its-kind concept demo showing a live downstream operation at 3.0GHz over a coaxial plant, showing the spectrum migration path continuing beyond 1.8 GHz. The demo consists of actual working hardware featuring a 3.0GHz concept amplifier, SC-QAMs, OFDM channels, and a 3.0GHz DOCSIS signal generator.SCTE TechExpo 2026 marks the public debut of AOI's QuantumWave? 25G Tunable SFP, the newest addition to the Quantum Bandwidth product family. As operators deploy DOCSIS 4.0 and Distributed Access Architectures (DAA), transport links between the CCAP or virtualized core, aggregation hubs, and Remote PHY/Remote MACPHY devices are increasingly outgrowing traditional 10G connectivity.QuantumWave gives operators a cost-effective, compact option for mid-haul and backhaul links. Dual-mode 10G/25G Operation: Configure for 10G or 25G NRZ in the same hot-pluggable SFP28 module, so capacity can grow without replacing hardware. Simplified Inventory: A narrow-linewidth C-band tunable laser covers 48 DWDM channels (ITU channels 16?63, 100 GHz spacing), so one part number replaces wavelength-specific spares.Extended Reach: Up to 40 km at 25G and up to 80 km at 10G on single-mode fiber, with an APD receiver and CDR with electronic dispersion compensation. Built for the Outside Plant: Operates from -20°C to 85°C with -40°C cold-start support and uses a copper upper cover for heat dissipation. Low Power: Under 4.5W on a single 3.3V supply.

historyItems.title: 新記憶體和 MicroLED 測試平台推出後泰瑞達股票成為焦點
historyItems.summary: 2026年9月，泰瑞達與美國GS微電子公司建立了多年合作夥伴關係，在矽谷建立了配備泰瑞達的半導體測試和評估中心，而泰瑞達還推出了Iris 100 microLED光學測試平台，並在印度班加羅爾開設了專注於半導體的辦事處。這些舉措共同擴展了泰瑞達在人工智慧、光學和印度不斷發展的晶片生態系統中的影響力，加強了其與下一代半導體設計、測試和製造工作流程的整合。接下來，我們將研究 Iris 100 microLED 測試發布可能如何影響泰瑞達的長期投資敘述和成長前景。
historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Stock In Focus After New Memory And MicroLED Test Platform Launches
historyItems.originalSummary: In September 2026, Teradyne and GS Microelectronics U.S. formed a multi-year partnership to build a Teradyne-equipped semiconductor test and evaluation center in Silicon Valley, while Teradyne also launched its Iris 100 microLED optical test platform and opened a semiconductor-focused office in Bengaluru, India. Together, these moves extend Teradyne's reach across AI, optical, and India's growing chip ecosystem, tightening its integration into next-generation semiconductor design, test, and manufacturing workflows. Next, we'll examine how the Iris 100 microLED test launch may influence Teradyne's long-term investment narrative and growth outlook.

historyItems.originalTitle: Aehr Test Systems Rises as Investors Revisit AI Order Momentum and Backlog
historyItems.originalSummary: FREMONT, CA / ACCESS Newswire / September 28, 2026 / Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ:AEHR), a leading provider of test and burn-in solutions for semiconductor devices used in artificial intelligence (AI), silicon photonics, data center, automotive, and industrial applications, today announced that President and CEO Gayn Erickson and CFO Chris Siu will be participating in the 18th Annual CEO Investor Summit being held Tuesday, October 13that the St. Regis Hotel, San Francisco, CA."We once again look forward to participating in this annual event and discussing with investors and shareholders Aehr's expanding role in enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices across a wide range of markets," said Mr. Erickson. "Aehr delivers complete turnkey solutions that improve the quality, reliability, and yield of semiconductors used in critical applications, including AI processors in cloud computing and data centers, silicon carbide devices in electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, gallium nitride for advanced power conversion, and silicon photonics for data centers, 5G infrastructure and optical input/output (I/O). We are seeing strong traction with AI processors in both wafer-level and package-level formats. They did this, the filing says, by doing drive-bys of the observers’ homes and, in the case of at least one observer, requiring that she be referred to secondary inspection any time she tries to cross the border until at least January 2027. "The government is treating people who exercise their First Amendment rights and seek to hold it accountable as criminal suspects, and that's what we're asking the court to stop,” says JoAnna Suriani, an attorney at Protect Democracy who is representing ICE observers in the case. The filing focuses on agents’ conduct during “Operation Catch of the Day,” an immigration enforcement surge in Maine this past January. It is part of a proposed class action brought in federal court in Maine by four observers: Elinor Hilton, Colleen Fagan, Polyxenia Pantos, and Carlyn Williams. It was filed under seal in September, and a redacted version was made public Friday. In particular, it describes how one DHS agent, referred to as “Agent J.C.” in the filing, used the Investigative Case Management (ICM) database, which the government describes as the case management system the ICE component Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) uses to document its investigations, to flag observers. According to the filings, J.C. created ICM records on at least six observers; the government puts the number of people at eight. He labeled two people he filmed at a Home Depot parking lot with “Threat to Law Enforcement, Professional Protestor,” according to the filing, and sent photos of them and others to a US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer so he could run a facial recognition search on them using an app called Mobile Query. On January 20, Pantos briefly watched and photographed an arrest in Portland, Maine, standing a few car lengths away beside their spouse's car. Hours later, per the filing, J.C. ran the car's plate and pulled a report on the owner—Williams—from Accurint, a LexisNexis database for law enforcement, which listed her address, phone numbers, and cohabitants. J.C. then allegedly circulated her photo to his team, asking, “Was this the protestor.” Another agent, per the filing, replied that it didn’t match the woman he had dealt with at the scene; J.C. then told colleagues he was "adding them in ICM now." According to the legal filing, that afternoon, J.C. called Williams on her cell phone, identifying himself only as "the Department of Homeland Security." According to Williams, he told her she "should encourage" her spouse, Pantos, "not to do anything like that in the future because people who are doing things like that might get added to a domestic terrorism watchlist." historyItems.originalSummary: NASA is streaming live coverage as it prepares for the arrival and docking of the agency's SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station.The SpaceX Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to dock at approximately 7 p.m. EDT. Dragon is designed to dock autonomously, and the crew aboard the spacecraft and the space station will monitor its approach to the forward port of the orbiting laboratory's Harmony module.When the hatches open about one hour and 45 minutes after docking, NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov will join the Expedition 75 crew for a long-duration science mission aboard the orbiting laboratory.Crew-13 launched earlier today at 11:10 a.m. from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.Contact:Mary W. historyItems.summary: 慧與週三上調了網路部門的成長前景，並宣布從雲端基礎設施公司 Vultr 獲得 12 億美元的訂單，在 Vultr 的美國資料中心部署 AMD Helios AI 機架系統。該公司表示，HPE 將 2027 財年網路部門營收成長預測從先前的 14% 至 17% 的預測上調至 10% 至 20% 左右。該公司表示，從長遠來看，HPE將其網路部門營收成長目標從2026財年到2029財年的複合年增長率提高到了十幾%，而先前的展望是2025財年到2028財年的年複合成長率為5%到7%。
historyItems.originalTitle: HPE stock closes at record high on growing networking orders, $1.2 billion AMD Helios order
historyItems.originalSummary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise raised its networking segment growth outlook on Wednesday and announced a $1.2 billion order from cloud infrastructure company Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI rack systems at Vultr's U.S. data centers. HPE lifted its fiscal 2027 networking segment revenue growth forecast to a range of high teens to low-20s percent, up from a previous forecast of 14% to 17%, the company said. Over a longer horizon, HPE lifted its networking segment revenue growth target to a high-teens percent compound annual growth rate spanning fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2029, compared with a prior outlook calling for 5% to 7% yearly growth over fiscal 2025 through fiscal 2028, the company said. The company expects the segment to maintain an operating margin in the mid-to-high 20s percent range from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029.

historyItems.summary: 慧與週三上調了網路部門的成長前景，並宣布從雲端基礎設施公司 Vultr 獲得 12 億美元的訂單，在 Vultr 的美國資料中心部署 AMD Helios AI 機架系統。該公司表示，HPE 將 2027 財年網路部門營收成長預測從先前的 14% 至 17% 的預測上調至 10% 至 20% 左右。該公司表示，從長遠來看，HPE將其網路部門營收成長目標從2026財年到2029財年的複合年增長率提高到了十幾%，而先前的展望是2025財年到2028財年的年複合成長率為5%到7%。
historyItems.originalTitle: HPE’s $1.2 billion order from Vultr puts its AI networking strategy to the test
historyItems.originalSummary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise raised its networking segment growth outlook on Wednesday and announced a $1.2 billion order from cloud infrastructure company Vultr to deploy AMD Helios AI rack systems at Vultr's U.S. data centers. HPE lifted its fiscal 2027 networking segment revenue growth forecast to a range of high teens to low-20s percent, up from a previous forecast of 14% to 17%, the company said. Over a longer horizon, HPE lifted its networking segment revenue growth target to a high-teens percent compound annual growth rate spanning fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2029, compared with a prior outlook calling for 5% to 7% yearly growth over fiscal 2025 through fiscal 2028, the company said. The company expects the segment to maintain an operating margin in the mid-to-high 20s percent range from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2029.

historyItems.originalTitle: RFK Jr. announces partnership with Dell Medical School to boost clinical trials in the US
historyItems.originalSummary: UT Austin's Dell Medical School will have a key role in new projects aimed at improving and expanding clinical trials in the United States, federal officials announced Wednesday. U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was joined by Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services administrator Mehmet Oz and other top health officials to unveil the new SURPASS initiative — an acronym for "Simulation-augmented, Real-time Platform Adaptive Seamless Trials." Kennedy said the goal was to modernize American clinical trial infrastructure to be able to compete with countries that are amping up medical innovation, including China and Australia. "The system we have today takes far too long, it costs too much and it asks too much of the patients," Kennedy said. SURPASS is funded by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) , an agency within HHS created under the Biden administration that invests in innovative research and "breakthrough technologies." With this initiative, the agency hopes to speed up the development of new disease treatments. "Today's clinical trial system often requires too many stops, too much duplicated infrastructure, and too much time before researchers can understand whether a trial is on the right track," said Daria Fedyukina, program manager for SURPASS, in a news release. Dell Medical School will be the "key academic partner" for two major projects announced as part of the SURPASS initiative. The first, known as STACK, intends to equip more research sites to take on clinical trials and make them more accessible to patients where they live, including in rural areas. The second, the COMMONS project, will develop a "national research data resource" which institutions across the country can access and contribute to. In addition to sharing data useful for future clinical trials, it aims to help institutions identify patients who might be a good fit for a project. Dell Medical School will be the first institution to contribute to and test COMMONS. Dell Medical School will dedicate resources from across UT to the efforts, including contributions from experts in computing, engineering and data science. Claudia Lucchinetti, the dean of Dell Medical School, said the projects align with the university's goals in opening the forthcoming Dell Medical Center — "bringing research closer to patients and making learning part of everyday care." "These projects will help build a lasting foundation for that work by connecting patients with appropriate trials, bringing participation closer to home and using real-world and digital data to better understand what works and for whom," Lucchinetti said in a news release.

historyItems.originalTitle: Planet Labs CEO on satellite launch: The first time we're launching TPUs into space
historyItems.originalSummary: Planet Labs PBC announced that Pelican-12, an updated second generation (Gen 2) high resolution Pelican?, has arrived at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida ahead of its launch aboard the upcoming Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission with SpaceX. Pelican-12 leverages key learnings from Pelican-11, which launched in July. Shipping less than three months later with updates to the payload and communication systems, Pelican-12 demonstrates Planet's end-to-end agile engineering.Like its predecessors, Pelican-12 will allow Planet to test and validate new technologies ahead of integration on future Planet spacecraft. Planet is working to test commercial data relay services onboard its constellations to minimize latency in its delivery of data to customers. This Pelican satellite is designed to support intersatellite communications using a steerable antenna, and aims to enable two-way communications at higher data rates than the 1 Mbps achieved in an initial demonstration in 2025.While Planet?s first generation (Gen 1) Pelicans are designed to capture 50 cm class imagery, Gen 2 Pelicans are designed to provide up to 30 cm class imagery - further improving use cases such as agricultural monitoring, critical infrastructure management, and natural disaster response. Pelican-12 is also equipped with the NVIDIA Jetson platform to accelerate on-orbit edge compute, a capability Planet demonstrated by running AI-driven, near real-time object detection onboard Pelican-4. By utilizing its onboard NVIDIA Jetson module, Pelican-12 will help Planet explore new ways to close the latency gap with real-time insights, reduce downlink costs, and continue building towards a future of planetary-scale Earth intelligence.

historyItems.title: 波音公司再獲 22 架 F-15EX 戰機訂單
historyItems.summary: 美國空軍已授予波音公司一份價值 23.8 億美元的合同，根據第 7 批生產另外 22 架 F-15EX Eagle II 飛機。在最新合約中，該公司於 8 月交付了第 3 批中的主力 F-15EX-22 飛機，並將在 2026 年交付更多飛機，並於本月早些時候選擇為美國海軍建造第六代 F/A-XX 戰鬥機。波音公司目前簽訂了全面生產 F-15EX 1 至 7 批的合同，預計將生產總共 120 架 F-15EX 戰鬥機，以取代服役中老化的 F-15C/D 飛機。這家美國製造商正在與美國空軍和五角大廈密切合作，將產量提高到每月兩架飛機。
historyItems.originalTitle: Boeing secures order for 22 more F-15EX fighters
historyItems.originalSummary: The US Air Force has awarded Boeing a $2.38-billion contract to produce an additional 22 F-15EX Eagle II aircraft under Lot 7. The latest award follows the company’s delivery of the lead F-15EX-22 aircraft under Lot 3 in August, with more to follow throughout 2026, as well as its selection to build the US Navy’s sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter earlier this month. With Boeing currently under contract for the full production of F-15EX Lots 1 through 7, it is now expected to produce a total of 120 F-15EX fighters to replace the service’s aging F-15C/D aircraft. The American manufacturer is closely collaborating with the US Air Force and the Pentagon to increase the production rate to two aircraft per month. "Lot 7 reflects a disciplined approach to executing available resources while balancing the realities affecting defense production," said Brig. Gen. Timothy Helfrich, portfolio acquisition executive for the Fighters and Advanced Aircraft Directorate. F-15EX Lots 1 To 7 The US Air Force first awarded Boeing a nearly $1.2-billion contract for eight F-15EX aircraft under Lot 1 in July 2020, with all eight aircraft delivered by June 2024 and entering initial operating capability the following month. The service subsequently ordered 12 aircraft under Lot 2 in 2021 and another 12 under Lot 3 in 2022. It later ordered 24 aircraft under Lot 4, 24 under Lot 5, and 18 under Lot 6, bringing the total number of aircraft under contract to 98 before the latest award. F-15EX production was disrupted when Boeing machinists at the company's St. Louis facility went on strike from August 4 to November 17, 2025. The disruption, along with broader inflation across the defense industrial base, was among the factors the Department of the Air Force said it accounted for in negotiating the Lot 7 agreement. Multirole Strike Fighter Building on the F-15 Eagle model, the F-15EX incorporates advanced avionics, digital backbone architecture, large-area displays, and enhanced survivability. With a 29,500-pound (13,300-kilogram) payload capacity, it can carry up to 12 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missiles (AMRAAMs) or an equivalent combination of large ordnance.

historyItems.title: 卡特彼勒計劃投資 10 億美元在北卡羅來納州桑福德建造製造工廠
historyItems.summary: 卡特彼勒週三宣布計劃在北卡羅來納州投資約 10 億美元，以擴大緊湊型建築設備的製造能力。該公司表示，計劃在桑福德建造一座新工廠，專門用於提高小型履帶式裝載機和伸縮臂叉裝機的產量。這項投資與卡特彼勒的 Cat Compact 策略相關，該策略針對小型承包商和成長型企業。該公司表示，這兩種機器類型均服務一系列行業，包括建築、園林綠化、農業和物料搬運。
historyItems.originalTitle: Caterpillar plans $1 billion investment in manufacturing facility in Sanford, North Carolina
historyItems.originalSummary: Caterpillar announced plans Wednesday to invest approximately $1 billion in North Carolina to expand manufacturing capacity for compact construction equipment. The company said it plans to construct a new Sanford facility dedicated to ramping up output of compact track loaders and telehandlers. The investment is tied to Caterpillar's Cat Compact strategy, which targets small contractors and growing businesses. Both machine types serve a range of industries, including construction, landscaping, agriculture and material handling, the company said.

historyItems.title: HPE 提高預測，從 Vultr 獲得 12 億美元的設備訂單
historyItems.summary: 惠普企業公司提高了其網路收入預測，並宣布從雲端公司 Vultr 獲得 12 億美元的訂單，發出了新的信號，表明該公司正從人工智慧的發展中受益。該公司去年透過收購瞻博網路擴大了網路業務，目前預計該細分市場在 2027 財年的銷售成長百分比將在十幾歲到二十幾歲之間。該公司也給出了較高十幾歲的長期銷售前景，營業利潤率為目標高達20多歲。如需了解更多信息，我們採訪了 HPE 首席財務官 Marie Myers。
historyItems.originalTitle: HPE Boosts Forecast, Gets $1.2 Billion Gear Order From Vultr
historyItems.originalSummary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. boosted its networking revenue forecast and announced a $1.2 billion order from cloud company Vultr, giving fresh signals that it's benefiting from the AI build-out.The company, which expanded its networking business by acquiring Juniper Networks last year, now expects that segment to range from the high teens to the low 20s in percentage sales growth during fiscal 2027. The company also gave a longer-range sales outlook in the high teens, with an operating margin target of as much as the high 20s. For more, we speak with Marie Myers, Chief Financial Officer at HPE.

historyItems.summary: 隨著第一波發布日的 Googlebook 硬體在短短幾天內登陸商店貨架，人們很容易認為開發工作可能會很平靜，而每個人都在等待市場的反應。相反，下一代 Googlebooks 的開發工作已經在全力進行中。就在「Coolum」——即將推出的英特爾酷睿系列 3 翻蓋式處理器（可能來自聯想）被發現幾天后，又一款開發板正式出現在 Chromium Gerrit 中。這款代號為「Blanc」的新裝置指向另一家製造商，為更主流、更容易使用的英特爾驅動的 Googlebook 奠定基礎。
historyItems.originalTitle: Googlebook Launches with Intel Core Ultra Series 3 Processors
historyItems.originalSummary: With the first wave of launch-day Googlebook hardware landing on store shelves in just a matter of days, it would be tempting to think development work might be quiet while everyone waits to see how the market reacts. Instead, work on the next generation of Googlebooks is already moving full steam ahead. Just days after ‘Coolum’ - an upcoming Intel Core Series 3 clamshell likely coming from Lenovo - was uncovered, yet another development board has officially popped up in the Chromium Gerrit. Codenamed ‘Blanc’, this new device points toward another manufacturer laying the groundwork for a more mainstream, accessible Intel-powered Googlebook. via the Chromium Gerrit Clamshell, convertible, or detachable? Whenever a brand-new board surfaces, the first big question is always form factor: are we looking at a traditional clamshell, a 2-in-1 convertible, or a detachable tablet like Lenovo’s upcoming Duet m? While it is still very early days for ‘Blanc’, the initial code provides some clear structural clues. The setup files account for standard active cooling fans, everyday USB-A and USB-C port layouts, and traditional laptop battery rails. Because there is no evidence of detachable magnetic connectors or specialized tablet-first thermal restrictions, ‘Blanc’ is shaping up to be a traditional clamshell laptop or a convertible 2-in-1 rather than a tablet/detachable. Aiming for mainstream Intel performance Under the hood, ‘Blanc’ is branching directly off Google’s ‘Ocelot’ baseboard, which is the reference platform for upcoming Intel Core Series 3 (Wildcat Lake) processors. That is a crucial distinction. During Google’s media event in New York City, the initial x86 Intel devices like the Lenovo Googlebook 15, Acer Googlebook 14, and the ultralight ASUS Googlebook 14 all came equipped with Intel’s top-tier Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) chips and $899+ price tags to match. ‘Blanc’ and the ‘Ocelot’ family represent the next tier down. Instead of chasing ultra-premium, bleeding-edge specs, these Core Series 3 machines are being designed for the high-volume, mainstream market. They will bring reliable multi-core processing, modern on-device AI acceleration for Gemini features, and long battery life at a price point that regular consumers and students will definitely enjoy. Looking ahead to 2027 Because ‘Blanc’ is literally in its very first week of public code commits, this is not a device you will see hitting Best Buy or the Google Store this fall. Taking a board from its earliest power configurations to retail certification usually takes anywhere from six to nine months, and Intel's Wildcat Lake hardware is firmly tracking toward early 2027. Still, seeing two separate Intel Core Series 3 laptops (‘Coolum’ and now ‘Blanc’) spin up alongside each other shows that hardware partners are already treating Googlebook as a long-term platform rather than a one-time trial. We will keep an eye on ‘Blanc’ as the code matures to see which OEM ultimately puts its logo on the lid.

historyItems.originalTitle: Constellation and Amazon Announce 20-Year Power Purchase Agreement Adding 190 Megawatts of Nuclear Capacity at Calvert Cliffs
historyItems.originalSummary: LUSBY, Md., September 30, 2026 --( BUSINESS WIRE )--Constellation (Nasdaq: CEG) and Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN) today announced a long-term agreement that will support the continued investment in and expansion of the Calvert Cliffs Clean Energy Center, Maryland's only nuclear plant and largest source of clean energy. The agreement will enable more than $3 billion in Maryland infrastructure investment, including state-of-the-art improvements across the entire 1,790-megawatt plant and approximately 190 megawatts in total of new, emissions-free generating capacity coming online between 2030 and 2032.

historyItems.originalTitle: Pause & Effects' wonderfully textured Thalassa Germanium Diodes Harmonic Overdrive gets a very significant format upgrade
historyItems.originalSummary: I’m very proud of this project - which had some influence from yours truly, while new friend Attila of Pause & Effects did all the heavy lifting. On our first encounter back in March of this year, I noted that while his pedals looked very neat and elegant - there was a degree of the generic about them, and they needed a certain something to elevate them to make them more memorable and recallable. It was Attila who first suggested using the Pause Symbol on the LED, but after a couple of fruitless attempts at that he almost gave up on that approach. I kind of strong-armed him into carrying on experimenting - and he veritably struck gold in that second phase. All of this has taken a while to perfect, and I feel that the results are well worth the time put into said project! Attila also extended the facia plate to full-length - which gives the pedal a more formidable and dominant look - and that blue-lit Pause Symbol on the LED is the cherry on top. And it’s all gelled together by the most gorgeous deep blue hue for this particular model - that matt / satin finish of blue has hidden depths to it - it looks utterly luxurious in the flesh so to speak. Of course the pedal would be no good if the internals and output didn’t match the brilliance of the new look. And those Germanium OA1150’s deliver a really beautifully harmonically textured output - leading to a wonderfully textured crunch at higher intensities. Note that you do get something of a noise floor when you crank both Volume and Gain, possibly could do with some further internal filtering - but sounds pretty spectacular as is. And you have proper Active Bass and Active Treble EQ Controls to fully sculpt and shape the output - where dialling both of those back and upping the volume delivers a mid boost when you need it - and of course the reverse for a Mid-scoop!. Controls - Volume, Gain, Active Bass ±18dB (cf around 70-80Hz), Active Treble ±18dB (cf around 3-4 kHz)

historyItems.title: Diodes 推出額定電流為 2 A 至 8 A 的汽車現場電鍍超級勢壘整流器
historyItems.summary: Chris Ruoff 於 2026 年 9 月 29 日發布，並在 Newswire、The Tech 下歸檔。 Diodes 公司推出了一系列汽車用現場電鍍超級勢壘整流器 (SBRFP) 裝置，包括額定電流為 2 A、3 A 和 8 A 的零件。 Diodes 表示，這些零件是同類肖特基和 PN 接面二極體的直接替代品，其低正向電壓和反向漏電流適合 DC-DC 轉換器、反極性保護電路、電池充電系統、汽車 LED 照明和傳輸控制系統。
historyItems.originalTitle: Diodes launches automotive field-plated Super Barrier Rectifiers rated from 2 A to 8 A
historyItems.originalSummary: Posted September 29, 2026 by Chris Ruoff & filed under Newswire , The Tech . Diodes Incorporated has introduced a family of field-plated Super Barrier Rectifier (SBRFP) devices for automotive use, including parts rated at 2 A, 3 A and 8 A. Diodes says the parts are drop-in replacements for comparable Schottky and PN junction diodes, and that their low forward voltage and reverse leakage suit DC-DC converters, reverse-polarity protection circuits, battery charging systems, automotive LED lighting and transmission control systems. Diodes says its patented field-plated rectifier technology, built on a metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) manufacturing process rather than the metal-semiconductor junction of a conventional Schottky rectifier, overcomes the limitations of both Schottky and PN junction diodes. The 8 A SBRFP8A60P5Q has a maximum forward voltage of 0.55 V at 8 A. A rectifier’s conduction loss is the product of its forward voltage and current, so a lower drop means less heat to remove at higher currents. The 2 A SBRFP2M60P1Q and 3 A SBRFP3M60SAFQ have maximum reverse leakage currents of 12 µA and 7 µA, respectively, at 25° C and a 60 V reverse voltage, according to their data sheets. Schottky leakage climbs steeply with temperature, and Diodes says the low leakage helps minimize the risk of thermal runaway under high-temperature operating conditions. Avalanche energy ratings reach up to 145 mJ, depending on the device. The data sheet lists that rating for the SBRFP2M60P1Q at an avalanche current of 2 A. Diodes puts the family’s avalanche capability at five to 10 times that of conventional Schottky rectifiers, which the company says lets the parts withstand surge events, load dumps and other transients common in automotive electrical systems. The SBRFP2M60P1Q comes in a PowerDI123 package, the SBRFP8A60P5Q in PowerDI5 and the SBRFP2M60SAFQ and SBRFP3M60SAFQ in SMAF. All four operate across a junction temperature range of -55° C to +175° C. In 1,000-piece quantities, pricing is $0.08 for the SBRFP2M60P1Q, $0.11 for the SBRFP2M60SAFQ, $0.13 for the SBRFP3M60SAFQ and $0.26 for the SBRFP8A60P5Q.

historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile Rises 5% as New Change-of-Control Severance Plan Fuels Buyout Speculation; SpaceX and Rocket Lab Tick Up
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) jumped 3% after its board adopted a change-of-control severance plan that retail traders read as a buyout signal despite no acquisition being disclosed. SpaceX (SPCX) and Rocket Lab (RKLB) each gained less than 1% in sympathy, but neither move shares ASTS's company-specific executive-filing catalyst. With a beta of 2.73 and no confirmed launch date for the next three BlueBird satellites, ASTS's inference-driven rally can reverse quickly. historyItems.originalTitle: College Students Flex Their Power in A.I. Investment Frenzy
historyItems.originalSummary: Thank you for your patience while we verify access. Fourteen years ago, a venture capital firm created a program for college students to invest in their peers, called Dorm Room Fund. Some dismissed the effort as risky and a little bit crazy. After all, could you really trust students to make good investments? Now the fund’s network has its tentacles all over the artificial intelligence boom. Dorm Room Fund’s alumni have gone on to establish major A.I. companies like the coding start-up Cursor and the defense tech company Shield AI. Others have become investors at top firms including Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Lightspeed Venture Partners. They share deals, advice and industry banter. This month, Dorm Room Fund raised a new $50 million fund to keep investing in companies created by college students and the 500 members of its alumni network. That is four times the size of its last fund, a sign of how much investor attitudes about the program have changed. Silicon Valley investors have long courted college students, including paying them to drop out, as Peter Thiel’s Thiel Fellowship famously does. But the wooing has gotten more aggressive in the A.I. boom, where dropouts and recent graduates are finding overnight success in growing numbers.

historyItems.originalTitle: NVIDIA Launches Open Agent Safety Platform to Secure Agents From Testing to Deployment
historyItems.originalSummary: NVIDIA today announced NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform , an open software platform and reference system design to strengthen AI security from agent testing to deployment, with full-stack governance and control across software and the hardware, compute and robotics systems that run agents. Recent security incidents have underscored the need to equip organizations with open, customizable tools that enforce more control over long-running agents. Across these incidents, the pattern is the same — the agent circumvented security controls at the application layer to complete its assigned task. “AI’s extraordinary potential for society will only be realized if we solve AI safety,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety. Safety and security require full-stack engineering. NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform brings together industry, researchers and public-sector organizations to share best practices, align on evaluation methods and foster international cooperation. Together, we can raise the bar for global AI safety.” Open Agent Safety Platform Adds Control Across the Full Agent Stack NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform enables full-stack governance and control across the software that runs agents, the hardware and compute layers that power their work, and the robotics systems that execute tasks in the physical world. Organizations can deploy elements of NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform according to their unique requirements. It includes NVIDIA OpenShell ™ secure runtime software that sets boundaries for agents running on CPUs. As agents take on more work across more systems, enterprises need an enforceable boundary outside of the model and agent harness. Now broadly available, OpenShell provides a secure runtime boundary for controlling how autonomous AI agents execute tasks across open and closed models. OpenShell delivers this protection with minimal overhead on NVIDIA Vera , the first purpose-built CPU for agentic AI. Together, OpenShell and Vera enable agents to operate securely while completing their work as quickly as possible. As open source software, OpenShell can also be extended to work with third-party compute platforms, including those from Arm and Intel . The NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform reference system design features NVIDIA Sentry , an out-of-band watchdog that runs on NVIDIA BlueField ® -4 DPUs to continuously monitor agent behavior. Sentry provides in-silicon security enforcement, meaning that if an AI agent attempts to move outside its software boundary, Sentry quarantines and stops it in milliseconds. Running on BlueField-4 DPUs, Sentry continuously monitors agent activity and enforces security policies independently in silicon. It combines threat detection, hardware-based agent governance and enforcement and data access protection from an isolated, out-of-band trust domain that is responsive in real time and invisible to agents and attackers. historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX launches its massive Starship rocket into orbit for the first time
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX launched its enormous Starship into orbit for the first time Monday and successfully delivered the most advanced Starlinks yet, but decided to cut short the flight. SpaceX said the spacecraft would reenter over the Pacific and splash down north of Hawaii three hours after blasting off from Texas. The company had been aiming for a 10-hour flight, spanning six full laps around Earth, to prove its readiness for NASA’s Artemis moon program. The spacecraft almost didn’t make it to orbit after one of its engines shut down too soon. But with everything else working well and the bad engine no longer needed, flight controllers decided after several tense minutes to proceed as planned. “Starship is orbital,” Mission Control announced to cheers. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated SpaceX on reaching orbit and “managing every step in a safe, responsible and especially inspirational way.” Founder Elon Musk’s showpiece rocket — the biggest and most powerful ever built — carried 26 of the latest and most advanced Starlink satellites to join the 11,000 older models already providing internet service. They popped out of the spacecraft one by one, drawing more cheers from the SpaceX crowds looking on from the launch site at Starbase, Texas. The decision to end the flight early came soon afterward. No reason was provided. It was Starship’s 14th full-scale launch from Texas’ southern tip in three years. The earlier test flights ventured no farther than the Indian Ocean halfway around the world, often crashing in flames and briefly skimming space. This time, SpaceX was intent on circling the globe from an altitude of 170 miles — not just once but six times over almost 10 hours, ending with a Pacific splashdown near Chile. While Starship achieved the proper orbit zipping along at 17,500 mph, flight controllers opted to play it safe and bring it back several hours sooner, after just a couple laps. The first-stage booster was never meant to return to the Starbase launch site either, instead dropping into the Gulf of Mexico within minutes of the morning liftoff. SpaceX wants to ensure that everything works before flying Starship back to Starbase. If the spacecraft breaks apart over land and rains debris onto people, “our popularity would diminish very rapidly,” Musk said at a business summit earlier this month. “That’s why we’re being extremely cautious here.” Depending on the findings from Monday’s orbital debut, the next Starship could return to the launch pad with giant mechanical arms grabbing the hovering spacecraft. If the catch works — Musk gives it even or slightly better odds — then SpaceX will refly the spacecraft by year’s end or early next year. The 407-foot rocket was designed from the start to be fully reusable — a key to lowering launch costs. SpaceX managed to salvage the last Starship from the Indian Ocean in July. Engineers modified the newly launched Starship’s heat shield based on hands-on inspections from the recovered spacecraft, which is being tugged back to Starbase.
